tui.authoring.promote_failed.note: {reason} is the registry's own English sentence (collision, missing name, rollback remainder); the wrapper is the only translated part.

tui.authoring.promote_mixed_plan.role: rehearsal line when one plan both overwrites and copies
tui.authoring.promote_mixed_plan.note: {replaced} names the account definitions that would be overwritten; {created} names the new copies. The overwrite comes first in the sentence and the notice is `warning` for the same reason as promote_replace_plan. `yes` stays literal.

tui.authoring.promote_plan.role: rehearsal line before a confirmed copy
tui.authoring.promote_plan.tone: plain, calm, explicit that nothing changed
tui.authoring.promote_plan.note: {names} is a comma-joined list of the definitions a confirmed call would copy into the account. `yes` stays a literal token. Never reads as a warning: copying is a normal, reversible-in-effect act.

tui.authoring.promote_receipt_created.note: {names} is the comma-joined list of definitions newly COPIED into the account. Never includes a replaced row: a replacement needs its own sentence (design round 1, D2).

tui.authoring.promote_receipt_keeps.note: The clause users get wrong (the origin conversation keeps launching its own row), split out so it survives whatever precedes it. Never dropped.

tui.authoring.promote_receipt_replaced.note: {names} is the comma-joined list of EXISTING account definitions this call overwrote. Printed only when something was replaced, so a copy-only receipt never implies a loss (design round 1, D2 / UX U1).

tui.authoring.promote_replace_plan.role: rehearsal line before a confirmed overwrite
tui.authoring.promote_replace_plan.tone: plain, direct, names what will be lost; leads the notice
tui.authoring.promote_replace_plan.note: {names} is a comma-joined list of the account definitions the confirmed call would OVERWRITE. This sentence is printed FIRST and as a `warning` notice (design round 1, D1): the destructive half must never read as an afterthought to the copies. `yes` stays literal.

tui.authoring.promote_usage.role: usage refusal for a reserved verb
tui.authoring.promote_usage.note: Printed when /agent promote or /team promote is typed wrong. {command} is a literal command path ('/agent promote'); the bracketed flags are the grammar, kept literal, including `as <new name>` — the rename spelling the collision refusal offers (review round 1, NIT-1 / UX U2).
